title: Gladys buys Cobb the horn Lucky Thompson wanted
summary: Gladys sends Cobb to Manning's to pick a used horn for $265, which turns out to be the one Lucky had chosen; Cobb also talks about his Selmer and Yamaha horns.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Gladys called me the next day. She said, Arnett, you need a horn, don't you? I said yes. She said, Go to Mannings and try that horn out and see if you like it. That's where Lucky was getting it. If you like it, call me up at home. Give my right hand to God.
I went to Mannings the next day, and I was suffering with mine, but I wasn't bugging nobody about it. I

went there and tried the horn, and I called her up from Mannings. And I say I like it. She said, go to Joe Glazer's office to pick up the check and come back and get your horn, and that's what I did. $265.00. Went to Joe Glazer's office on 5th Avenue, come back to Mannings, pick my horn up and got in (inaudible) studio (inaudible), and Lucky recognized the horn by serial number, and he said I run down (inaudible). And I didn't even know that was his horn that he had picked.
Oh, he got mad at me. He told me I was a Tom this and -- Uncle Tom. I don't even know this is his horn, Ellen. Gladys told me to go over and try one out.

But, see, what had happened, Lucky and his wife done give her a fit, so she said, the heck with him, and, you know, Gladys is cold. She was cold when she want to be cold. So she said, I'll show him something. That's what she said.
Arnett, what would that horn have been worth new?
What would that horn -- you said it was 265.00.
It was a used horn. It's second hand.
What would it have been worth new
Oh, so it was a very good buy.
Yeah, because my wife bought me one Christmas '47 for 500.00 in Detroit. I got it now, and that one I won't get rid of.
What kind of horn was it?
I bought one in Paris, and this is the Yamaha, endorsed that, got that for nothing. But I got to keep it because I'm selling them for the Yamaha people.
